subject: Re: Warning: value in right-hand-side-only variable is NA or NaN

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Warning: value in right-hand-side-only variable is NA or NaN
parts:
Dear Dali,

Before opening up your code, let me more quickly offer suggestions for how you can debug this issue yourself.  A right-hand-side only variable is a variable that appears only on the right-hand side of model declarations and never on the left-hand side.  This is often the case for explanatory variables.  For example, in 

a ~ dnorm(0, sd = 1000)
b ~ dnorm(0, sd = 1000)
sigma ~ dunif(0, 100)
for(i in 1:n) {
y[i] ~ dnorm(a + b*x[i], sd = sigma)
}

x[i] is a right-hand-side only variable because it is used as an explanatory variable but does not itself have a prior or a deterministic declaration.

You can use the model object to determine where you have NA or NaN values.  Build the model with nimbleModel.  (If you have been using nimbleMCMC to skip over nimbleModel, simply use the same code, data, constants, and/or inits in a call to nimbleModel, with the exception that inits can't be set up for multiple chains but should rather be a list of named model variables.) 

Then, inspect variables in your model.  For example, 

model <- nimbleModel(code, data = data, constants = constants, inits = inits) # same arguments as nimbleMCMC
model$x # look at x

In this way you can identify which variables contain NAs and/or NaNs.  Often it means that the data or constants are incomplete or incorrectly set up.

Can you please try these approaches (or let us know if you already have) and then if you are still stuck let us know and someone can run your code?

If you haven't yet dug into our user manual at r-nimble.org, that can also be a helpful source.

HTH
Perry
